messages:
maria: Heads up — ACME Support flagged that when an engineer rapidly switches org/workspace in the console they briefly see billing/usage graphs from another org. Screenshot attached in thread. :eyes:
kevin: yikes. repro steps? does it require super fast switching or any filter change?
maria: repro steps I followed:
1) open console -> billing tab for org A
2) open new tab, switch to org B dashboard fast (click org switcher twice)
3) go back to first tab and refresh dashboard -> you can see org B's aggregated usage for ~1–2s before the query re-runs
kevin: interesting. sounds like a stale in-memory cache or websocket broadcast race. any recent PRs touching dashboard store or router?
maria: pasted the timeline: deploy-bot shows a deploy 34m before reports: "deploy-bot: deploy #4723 to console-svc succeeded (main -> prod)"
deploy-bot: deploy #4723 started by @lisa — release note: "dashboard-route-mux: prefetch workspace metadata to reduce cold loads"
kevin: that prefetch change could be the culprit — if we prefetch and stash a workspace id on a shared singleton it could leak between tabs/workspaces. can you grab console logs for that timeframe? look for "workspace_prefetch" events.
maria: logs show at t=12:03:45: "workspace_prefetch: ctx=global, workspaceId=org-b-345" then at t=12:03:46 user in org-a-111 did query and omitted workspace variable so server defaulted to ctx.workspaceId.
kevin: can you paste the GraphQL request payload?
maria: here (sanitized):
```
POST /graphql
{
  query: "query GetBilling($start,$end){ billing(start:$start,end:$end){ total } }",
  variables: { "start":"2026-03-15","end":"2026-03-16" }
  // note: no workspaceId in variables
}
```
kevin: OK that matches. server is relying on request context instead of explicit variables if client omits workspaceId. The prefetch put the wrong workspaceId into the shared request context for that user session.
tara: probable race in request context propagation across tabs. Our per-session singleton is being mutated by prefetch. That aligns with the prefetch PR — it writes ctx.workspaceId at top-level rather than thread-local.
jonathan: from product perspective this is a severity 1 privacy exposure risk. customers seeing other org metrics is unacceptable. We need containment + rollback plan.
kevin: suggested immediate mitigations:
- flip feature flag `dashboard-namespace-prefetch` off in prod (fast rollback)
- block the prefetch codepath to write to a thread-local context (or attach workspaceId to the request object directly)
- add server-side guard: require `workspaceId` variable for billing queries and reject/return 400 if missing when user has >1 workspace access
- run a targeted audit of cache keys and websocket broadcast topics to ensure they include workspace scoping.
jonathan: agree. also we should notify security and privacy. open a support banner for ACME and any customers we've found affected.
lisa: toggled the ff in prod (done). I'll watch metrics and error logs. deploy-bot: feature flag flip recorded by @lisa — dashboard-namespace-prefetch=false.
maria: after flag flip I retried repro — cannot reproduce. no cross-org data visible.
kevin: next steps, short-term: revert PR 4723 or patch it to avoid writing to global ctx (I can put up a hotfix). long-term: add a unit/system test that does fast tab-switching and asserts no cross-workspace queries appear in logs.
tara: I'll add an integration test to the console e2e harness and a synthetic monitor that runs every 5m for workspace isolation checks (query history + telemetry anomalies).
jonathan: UX/rollout note — the prefetch was intended to speed cold loads; we need rollout UX that stages the prefetch by session and never writes to global singletons. consider canarying in one org only.
kevin: opened PR #4740 with hotfix (patch to write workspaceId to request-scoped context). linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4740
maria: created issue PLAT-2345 for root cause + postmortem: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-2345
kevin: will monitor for leaked metrics in logs and run a sweep for any other endpoints that implicitly rely on ctx.workspaceId.
tara: adding telemetry ticket to ensure our per-route traces include explicit workspaceId dimension (so we can detect cross-tenant anomalies automatically).
jonathan: timeline: hotfix -> 1h, tests + synthetic monitors -> 48h, full postmortem & customer communications -> 72h. Assign owners?
maria: owning customer comms, kevin owning hotfix, tara owning tests/monitoring, lisa to verify flag/metrics.
kevin: quick note — we should also run a small audit script to search logs for patterns of 2 different workspace ids within same session id in last 24h. I'll run that and paste results.
maria: thanks all. filing the immediate incident note in #incidents after we confirm scope. :white_check_mark:
kevin: preliminary audit shows 12 sessions in last 24h with quick workspace flips; only 1 session produced visible cross-org billing query (the ACME report). I'll post a full list in the incident doc.
lisa: leaving monitoring on for 2h, will escalate if anything else pops up.
jonathan: ok, close loop once postmortem draft is up.
